content.text:
**Sanmina (SANM) — filing review as of 2026-11-10**

**Primary sources used**
- **S1**: SEC **8-K / Exhibit 99.1** press release, **published 2026-11-09** (quarter ended 2026-10-03). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000044/sanmina_exx991xoctober32026.htm))  
- **S2**: SEC **10-Q** for quarter ended 2026-06-27, **published 2026-07-27** per supplied filing metadata. Liquidity, debt, and covenant language are in the filing. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000037/sanm-20260627.htm))

**What the latest filings say**
- FY26 was strong: revenue **$14.53B**, CFO **$944M**, FCF **$541M**, and ending cash **$1.68B** in the Q4 release. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000044/sanmina_exx991xoctober32026.htm))
- The post-quarter debt amendment matters: the 8-K says Amendment No. 5 **extends maturity of the revolver, Term Loan A, and delayed-draw facility to 2031**, resets amortization, and keeps the liens/guarantees in force. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000044/sanm-20261027.htm))
- The prior 10-Q showed total debt of **$2.172B**, with **$1.957B** long-term after current portion, and a fiscal maturity ladder that still had a **2030 lump** in the then-current schedule. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000037/sanm-20260627.htm))
- That same 10-Q said liquidity included **$1.8B cash**, **$1.5B revolver capacity net of borrowings/LCs**, **$600M Term Loan A availability**, and **$71M foreign short-term facilities**; it also noted receivable sales are an additional liquidity source but **subject to approval and not assured**. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000037/sanm-20260627.htm))
- Covenant language is present, but the filing only says the facilities contain a **maximum leverage ratio covenant** and a **minimum interest coverage covenant**; it does **not** provide stressed headroom in the excerpts retrieved. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000037/sanm-20260627.htm))

**Supported vs. unsupported assumptions**
- **Supported:** the company produced strong cash, has meaningful liquidity, and the 2030 maturity pressure on the old schedule was materially improved by the later amendment. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/897723/000089772326000044/sanmina_exx991xoctober32026.htm))
- **Unsupported / still needs proof:** a **50% share-price recovery case** is not yet source-supported from the filings alone; the valuation would require a defensible cash-flow/earnings bridge, current dilution math, and a fresh market-price anchor.  
- **Unsupported / incomplete:** exact **covenant headroom**, **recurring post-ZT cash conversion**, and any **receivable-sale run-rate** after the latest quarter are not fully evidenced in the retrieved excerpts.  
- **Unsupported / incomplete:** I did not retrieve a primary-source **comparable historical price** or a 5-year trading reference from SEC/Sanmina/Nasdaq in this pass.

**Concise verdict**

**What the latest filings show**
- In **S1 (10-Q, filed 2026-11-04)**, Vishay reported **$1.140B cash and cash equivalents**, **$735.5M total debt**, and **$409.7M net cash and short-term investments (debt)** at **2026-10-03**. It also reported **$314.8M** cash from operations for the first nine fiscal months of 2026 and **$74.8M** revenue for the latest quarter. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))
- S1 also says the company used part of the June/July 2026 equity-offering proceeds to **fully repay the revolver balance**, leaving **$0** outstanding on the credit facility at 2026-10-03; the 2030 convertibles remained outstanding. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))
- In **S2 (8-K, filed 2026-07-01)**, Vishay disclosed the **$50/share common-stock offering**, expected net proceeds of about **$830.3M**, and stated the proceeds would be used for growth initiatives and to reduce borrowings under the senior secured credit facility. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000114036126027081/ny20076868x4_8k.htm))

**Evidence for recovery**
- Liquidity improved materially after the equity raise: the 10-Q shows the revolver was paid down, cash rose, and net cash flipped positive versus year-end 2025. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))
- Management says free cash flow in the first nine months of 2026 improved versus the prior-year period and expects stronger cash generation after a period of elevated capex, though it warns fourth-quarter free cash flow will be pressured by a planned securitization reduction. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))
- Revenue in the latest quarter was higher than both the immediately prior quarter and the prior-year quarter, indicating some operating momentum. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))

**Counterevidence / unresolved risks**
- The 10-Q explicitly says fourth-quarter free cash flow should be **negative** due to a planned reduction in the receivables securitization program, and near-term cash generation remains tied to elevated capex. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))
- The filings do **not** provide a full stressed covenant headroom analysis, and the revolver’s availability is described as subject to covenant limits; that is not the same as fully underwritten spare liquidity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))
- The 2030 notes remain outstanding, and future conversion settlement could require cash and/or stock at the company’s election, so dilution and refinancing remain live considerations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))

**Unsupported assumptions to avoid**
- Assuming the latest quarter’s revenue growth means the business is in a durable uptrend. The filing only supports a **single-quarter** comparison, not a full-cycle turnaround. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))
- Assuming the equity raise permanently solves leverage. The filing supports reduced near-term debt, not an all-cycle de-leveraging thesis. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))
- Building a valuation from unverified forward FCF multiples or post-2026 margin expansion. No filing here supports those forecast inputs. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/103730/000010373026000080/form10q.htm))

**Bottom line:** the latest filings show **better liquidity and improved recent operating cash flow**, but they do **not** yet support a clean, fully underwritten recovery case with enough evidence for valuation or a high-conviction long thesis.
